idea.body: A multi-step word problem is really several one-step problems stacked in order. Read the whole problem first, and find what it is actually asking for. Work out one step at a time, using the result of each step as the start of the next. Watch for two traps: a number that never actually answers the question, and steps that only come out right in the order they happened. A garden with 4 rows of 9 seeds, minus 12 given away: multiply first for 36, then subtract 12, for 24 seeds left.

workedExample.prompt: A workshop has 25 screws. It buys 15 more, then gives away 8. How many screws are left?
steps: Read the whole problem before calculating anything.
Add the newly bought screws first: 25 plus 15 is 40.
Then subtract the ones given away: 40 minus 8 is 32.

ways.name: Work forward, step by step
ways.when: Use this for most multi-step problems, taking the actions in the order they happen.
steps: Read the whole problem before calculating anything.
Do the first action and write down the result.
Use that result as the start of the next action.
Repeat until every action in the problem is done.
ways.example: A workshop has 25 screws. It buys 15 more, then gives away 8. How many are left?
ways.trap: Doing the actions out of the order they happened in the story.

ways.name: Bar model
ways.when: Use this when the relationships between numbers are hard to picture in your head.
steps: Draw one bar for the amount after everything that joins has been added.
Shade the part that stays, and leave unshaded the part that leaves.
The shaded length is your answer.
ways.example: A workshop has 25 screws. It buys 15 more, then gives away 8. How many are left?
ways.trap: Shading the wrong part of the bar, so the shaded length does not match what stays.

figure.alt: A bar model of one piece per 4 screws: 8 of 10 pieces shaded to show 32 screws kept, 2 unshaded for 8 given away.

frames.caption: Draw one bar for the total.
The shaded length is your answer.

ways.name: Find the net change first
ways.when: Use this when a story has one starting amount, plus some gains and losses mixed together.
steps: Add up everything that joins the starting amount.
Add up everything that leaves the starting amount.
Subtract the total that leaves from the total that joins, for the net change.
Add that net change to the starting amount.
ways.example: A workshop has 25 screws. It buys 15 more, then gives away 8. How many are left?
ways.trap: Using this shortcut on a problem where one step changes what a later step even means.

ways.name: Underline the numbers you need
ways.when: Use this when a story includes an extra number that never answers the question.
steps: Read the question first and decide exactly what it is asking for.
Underline only the numbers that feed into that answer.
Ignore any number that is mentioned but never used in a calculation.
Work through the underlined numbers in story order.
ways.example: A rover has 25 screws and weighs 12 kilograms. It buys 15 more screws, then gives away 8. How many screws are left?
ways.trap: Using every number in the story, including one that was never needed for the question asked.

bank.prompt: A game world starts with 24 creatures. 15 more spawn in. Then 9 are defeated. How many creatures are left?
explanation: First add the new creatures: 24 plus 15 is 39.
Then subtract the defeated ones: 39 minus 9 is 30.
The steps have to happen in the order they are described.
bank.useAgain: when a count changes twice in a row, once up and once down.
hints: Work through the two changes in the order they happened.
Use the result of the first step as the starting point for the second step.
bank.socraticHint: Would adding the gain and the loss together first, before touching the start, give the same final answer?

bank.prompt: An aquarium ends the week with 18 fish. During the week, 6 fish were moved to another tank, after 10 new fish had been added. How many fish were there at the start of the week?
explanation: Work backwards from the end: undo the move first, since it happened last. 18 plus 6 is 24.
Then undo the addition, since it happened first: 24 minus 10 is 14.
Working backwards undoes each step in the reverse of the order it happened.
bank.useAgain: when the ending amount is known and the starting amount needs to be found by undoing each step in reverse.
hints: Undo the steps in the opposite order from how they happened.
Undo addition with subtraction, and undo subtraction with addition, one step at a time.
bank.socraticHint: Should the last thing that happened be undone first, or the first thing that happened?
